$comment: Gate 5 — every grammar node type the extractor consumes must map to exactly ONE Roslyn
SyntaxKind at the same byte span, or be listed here with its disambiguator.
This is the INVERSE of the enum-emission audit: that finds a declared value never
emitted; this finds one node type carrying two meanings. A correctly-positioned node
with the wrong kind is invisible to recall, completeness and error counts alike.
A grammar bump that changes either entry is a NAMED gate failure, never a silent
v1.2 adds shapeVariants — the MIRROR IMAGE of the allowlist above. `allowed` covers one
NODE TYPE carrying two MEANINGS. `shapeVariants` covers one CONSTRUCT emitted as two TREE
SHAPES. Neither loses a row; both corrupt a column, and neither is findable by any count.
Found by cs-impl reading node-types.json, prompted by the grammar-field-read gate.
The per-regime narrative keys below (fork8Audit, fork11Audit) are prose for a human.
This is the one a tool parses, so that advancing the pin and advancing the verdict are
a single edit that bless() can check. A refusal that depends on someone remembering to
re-run the audit is not a refusal.
auditStatus.meaning: 38 extractor-consumed node types carry more than one Roslyn meaning. Each needs either an allowlist entry naming its VERIFIED disambiguator, or a defect. Until then bless() refuses to store any DRIFT_ONLY claim, and refuses everything if the pin and the blessed regime differ.

triageProgress.method: group each ambiguous node type's occurrences by the Roslyn kind that discriminates them, and read what WE emitted at those spans. A column DISAMBIGUATES when its value sets are pairwise DISJOINT across the groups.
triageProgress.itShortlistsItDoesNotAdjudicate: the CONFLATED bucket still contains instrument artefacts — binary_expression is in it because one group's best-fit row is not an expressions row, so operatorString is dropped as a candidate rather than found to overlap. Entries are verified ONE AT A TIME against the fact base before a verdict is recorded here.

verifiedSoFar.record_declaration: DISAMBIGUATED by cs_type.typeCategory RECORD / RECORD_STRUCT via hasAnonymousToken(node,'struct'). VERIFIED.
verifiedSoFar.file_scoped_namespace_declaration: scope-setting sibling, not a container. VERIFIED; shapeVariant 5.
verifiedSoFar.accessor_declaration: CONFLATED. See CS-ORACLE-4 below. VERIFIED by hand at properties/Indexers.cs:49.
verifiedSoFar.type_parameter_constraint: DISAMBIGUATED for 5 of 6 constraint kinds, VERIFIED BY EXACT COUNTS against Roslyn over 302 fixtures: ClassConstraint 16=16, StructConstraint 14=14, ConstructorConstraint 11=11, RefStructConstraint 7=7. TypeConstraint 53 reconciles as 39 constraintTypeCount + 12 hasNotNullConstraint + 2 unmanaged — and the 2 are CS-ORACLE-6. The triage first read this NOT_EMITTED, which was the instrument: cs_type_parameter has NO startLine, so it can never join a span index.
verifiedSoFar.ref_type: DISAMBIGUATED. Its two meanings live in DIFFERENT relations — cs_variable.refKind (REF, REF_READONLY) for `ref int`, and cs_type_parameter.hasAllowRefStructConstraint for `allows ref struct`, which matched Roslyn 7=7. NOT_EMITTED was a span artefact, not a gap.
verifiedSoFar.yield_statement: NOT_EMITTED **BY DESIGN**. There is no cs_statement relation: the schema models expressions, blocks and variables. `yield return`'s operand appears with rootContext=YIELD_VALUE; `yield break` has no operand and so has no row. Recorded so NOT_EMITTED is never read as a gap here.
verifiedSoFar.goto_statement: NOT_EMITTED BY DESIGN, same reason — GotoCase / GotoDefault / Goto are statement kinds and statements are not rows.

triageProgress.remaining: 33 of 38 still need a verified disambiguator or a defect. Blessing is mechanically blocked by auditStatus.verdict until then.
triageProgress.whyNameIsNotADisambiguator: accessor_declaration first passed as 'DISAMBIGUATED BY methods.name' — a getter is called get_Foo and a setter set_Foo. True, trivial, and not a kind: a consumer switches on methodKind, not on a name. Excluding user-chosen identifiers is what surfaced CS-ORACLE-4. Language SYNTAX (operatorString, literalValue, unaryFixity) stays a candidate, because a token is determined by the construct while a name is determined by whoever wrote the code.
triageProgress.aWholeBucketWasTheInstrument: the NOT_EMITTED bucket held 4 entries and NONE was a parser gap: two are relations with no startLine or spans that do not coincide, and two are constructs the schema deliberately does not model. A verdict of 'we emit nothing here' must be read against WHAT THE SCHEMA CLAIMS TO EMIT before it is read as absence.

allowed.disambiguator: child is a spread (`..expr`) -> SpreadElement, else ExpressionElement
parent is conditional_access_expression -> index binding, else collection expression
allowed.assertion: ZERO-ROW. Resolved by the 0.23.5 grammar; retained so a regression to the 0.23.1 behaviour surfaces as a named failure rather than as silently misclassified rows.

shapeVariants.shapeA: class P(int a) : Base(a) — FLAT: identifier and argument_list are SIBLINGS in the base_list
shapeVariants.shapeB: record R(int X) : Parent(X) — WRAPPED in primary_constructor_base_type
shapeVariants.damageIfMissed: baseTypeName becomes 'Parent(X)' — a name no using scope resolves — and hasPrimaryConstructorArguments is false, losing the invocation entirely
shapeVariants.rule: handle BOTH shapes; assert baseTypeName never contains '('

shapeVariants.shapeA: params object[] a — wrapped in a `parameter` node
shapeVariants.shapeB: params int[] d — NOT wrapped; FLAT siblings of parameter_list, which declares name and type as MULTIPLE FIELDS on itself for this case
shapeVariants.damageIfMissed: the parameter is DROPPED ENTIRELY. params is in string.Format, every logging call, and most assertion helpers.
shapeVariants.rule: scan parameter_list for the flat form; assert parameterCount equals the declared arity

shapeVariants.shapeA: scoped Span<int> f — wraps the TYPE in scoped_type
shapeVariants.shapeB: scoped ref int g — emits a `modifier`
shapeVariants.damageIfMissed: isScoped false, losing a LIFETIME constraint so a ref struct appears free to escape; and completeTypeName becomes 'scoped System.Span<int>', a keyword glued to a type name
shapeVariants.rule: handle BOTH shapes; assert no completeTypeName starts with a contextual keyword

shapeVariants.shapeA: int x = 5 — the declarator has a `name` FIELD
shapeVariants.shapeB: var (a, b) = e — a `tuple_pattern` CHILD REPLACES the name field, so childForFieldName('name') returns NULL
shapeVariants.damageIfMissed: cs_variable row with an empty name and a deconstructionIndex that never fires; the bound identifiers a and b are lost entirely
shapeVariants.rule: branch on the presence of the tuple_pattern child, not on the name field; assert no cs_variable row has an empty name
shapeVariants.introducedBy: fork.patch — variable_declaration split on implicit_type, which moved the tuple form to an aliased _tuple_variable_declarator
shapeVariants.sameClassAs: the childForFieldName('parameters') null that reported 0 primary constructors

shapeVariants.shapeA: tree-sitter: `file_scoped_namespace_declaration` spans ONLY the directive — 33 characters, `namespace Fixtures.Ported.Blocks;` — and the declarations that follow are its SIBLINGS
shapeVariants.shapeB: Roslyn: `FileScopedNamespaceDeclaration` spans the WHOLE REST OF THE FILE — 9,375 characters in the same fixture — and those declarations are its CHILDREN
shapeVariants.damageIfMissed: an extractor that derives namespace by CONTAINMENT finds no type inside the node and gives every type an EMPTY namespace. 115 of 302 category fixtures use a file-scoped namespace, so declarationScopeKey would be wrong on the majority of them while every row count stayed right.
shapeVariants.rule: a file-scoped namespace SETS THE SCOPE FOR SUBSEQUENT SIBLINGS; it is not a container. VERIFIED correct in cs-type-extractor.ts (`scope = namespaceFrame(child, enclosing); continue;`). Recorded so a refactor to containment is a named failure.
shapeVariants.foundBy: the fork11 full-grammar audit, as a CONSUMED-BUT-NEVER-JOINED entry — the spans differ so wildly the two sides never met.

gateAssertion: for each shapeVariant, a fixture must exercise BOTH shapes and the emitted columns must agree. A fixture covering one shape passes while the other silently corrupts a column — which is how all three reached a 9,607-file corpus undetected.

scope.rule: injectivity applies to node types that denote a CONSTRUCT, not to leaf TOKENS
scope.why: a leaf token has no children to misclassify. What varies across its occurrences is the ENCLOSING construct — and naming the enclosing construct is what this audit DOES, not what it audits.

excludedByName.identifier: a bare name; the enclosing Roslyn node varies by position BY DEFINITION (measured: 25 leaf occurrences, 0 non-leaf)

scope.neverASilentFilter: exclusions are named with their reason, because a silent filter is how a real violation gets excluded later
scope.foundBy: the fork8 audit's first run, which reported identifier as a violation (TypeParameter / VariableDeclarator / IdentifierName, empty intersection). A false positive, and a scoping defect in the audit rather than in the grammar.

fork8Audit.ranAt: step 3 of the fork8 sequence, BEFORE any blessing, as ruled
fork8Audit.theRuleUnderExamination: fork rule 8 aliases _object_creation_generic_type to generic_name, so the node type is unchanged and only the provenance differs — the element_binding_expression shape
fork8Audit.structuralFinding: NOT a shapeVariant. generic_name is seq(identifier, type_argument_list); _object_creation_generic_type is prec.dynamic(2, seq(identifier, type_argument_list)) — identical children in identical order, only the precedence differs. node-types.json confirms generic_name's children are unchanged.
fork8Audit.injectivityFinding: CLEAN. All 7 occurrences map to Roslyn GenericName, including the one whose parent is object_creation_expression. Roslyn also uses ONE kind for both positions, so there is nothing to disambiguate.
fork8Audit.verdict: no allowlist entry needed, no shapeVariant entry needed. cs-impl was right to flag it and the answer is that it is safe.

fork11Audit.ranAt: step 3 of the fork11 sequence, BEFORE any blessing, as ruled
fork11Audit.whatChanged: fork rules 9-12 landed as three commits, each bumping the regime in the SAME commit. node-types.json gained and lost NOTHING: 225 named types before and after. Four types changed SHAPE — element_access_expression, invocation_expression, member_access_expression, prefix_unary_expression — which are exactly the four the new rules touch.
fork11Audit.scopeOfTheFork8Entry: the fork8 audit above examined ONE RULE, not the grammar. Its `violationsAfterScoping: 0` is a statement about fork rule 8 and nothing else. This entry is the FIRST FULL-GRAMMAR run, so its numbers are a new measurement and NOT a regression from zero. Reading 0 -> 38 as a fork11 regression would be wrong.
fork11Audit.instrument: ../parser-oracle/csharp/injectivity-audit.ts — the audit is now a SCRIPT. It was a hand procedure whose result was typed into this file as prose, and three regime bumps landed in one day.
fork11Audit.method: join tree-sitter named nodes to Roslyn nodes on EXACT (startByte, length); a node type is injective iff at least one Roslyn kind is present at EVERY occurrence.
fork11Audit.verdict: PENDING_TRIAGE, not clean. 38 consumed node types carry more than one Roslyn meaning. Most are expected one-to-many families whose disambiguator is a token ON the node — record_declaration -> RECORD/RECORD_STRUCT is VERIFIED correct via hasAnonymousToken(node,'struct'). Each of the 38 needs either an allowlist entry naming its VERIFIED disambiguator, or a defect. Blessing must not treat this as green.

oneConfirmedMisparse.repro: src/test-data/csharp/categories/.../AsyncAsIdentifier.cs — `int await = 1; int result = await + 1;` in a NON-async method
oneConfirmedMisparse.fork11: await_expression whose operand is the unary `+1`
oneConfirmedMisparse.consequence: the identifier reference to the local `await` is lost and a spurious await expression is emitted. No ERROR node, no count moves — a coherent misparse, which only an oracle can see.
oneConfirmedMisparse.ownedBy: cs-impl (grammar). Handed over with this repro; not fixed here.
oneConfirmedMisparse.note: `await` is contextual and reserved ONLY inside an async method. The fixture exists because cs-fixtures built it to probe exactly this.

joinCoverageIsNot100.measured: 97,345 of 129,215 named nodes joined — 75%. 29 CONSUMED node types never joined at all, so this audit says NOTHING about them.
joinCoverageIsNot100.why: Roslyn puts preprocessor directives and comments in TRIVIA, not in DescendantNodes(), so preproc_* / comment / shebang_directive can never join. `expression`, `type` and `unary_expression` are SUPERTYPES and are never a real node's type. The rest are structural containers whose extents differ.
joinCoverageIsNot100.rule: an unaudited type is UNAUDITED, never clean. Reporting 130 injective without this list would overstate what was checked.

errorsInTheInstrument: UNION instead of INTERSECTION. Roslyn nests nodes at identical spans — an argument `typeof(T)` is an Argument whose child TypeOfExpression starts and ends at the same byte. Counting every kind seen at a span reported 72 violations, including typeof_expression, which is TypeOfExpression at every single occurrence. A flood costs what a miss costs: nobody triages 72, and the real entries hide in it.

SCOPE TAKEN FROM THE WRONG FILE. extractor-grammar-reads.json records (nodeType, accessor, name) FIELD reads — 75 types — and answers 'does this field exist?'. Used as a consumption filter it excluded invocation_expression (3,580 occurrences) and member_access_expression (4,147) as 'not consumed'. The scope note in this file says a silent filter is how a real violation gets excluded later; that is exactly what it had become. Scope is now derived from the extractor SOURCE, intersected with the grammar's named types.

THE 32,767-CHARACTER LIMIT. The first run called parser.parse(src) directly and died with 'Invalid argument'. The audit now mirrors CSharpParser's callback path using the SAME constants read from csharp-constants.ts, so it sees the tree the extractor sees and not a differently-parsed one.

A VACUOUS CLEAN RESULT. The regime-injectivity sweep that preceded this run named a ref that does not exist; the pipeline died and still printed 'none'. Every refusal path in the script is now exit 2 with a reason — zero fixtures, zero joined spans, a missing oracle binary.

firstDefectFromTriage.repro: properties/Indexers.cs:49 — `public int this[bool flag] { get => flag ? 1 : 0; init => byIndex[0] = value; }`
firstDefectFromTriage.vocabulary: CsMethodKind has PROPERTY_GET, PROPERTY_SET, PROPERTY_INIT, INDEXER_GET, INDEXER_SET — and NO INDEXER_INIT
firstDefectFromTriage.consequence: an indexer's `init` accessor is indistinguishable BY KIND from its `set`. `init` is assignable only during object initialization; `set` is assignable always. A consumer switching on methodKind reads a write-once indexer as freely writable. The extractor KNOWS it is an init — the name says so — and the vocabulary has nowhere to put it: the parts are right and the structure is absent.
firstDefectFromTriage.owner: cs-impl — the enum value and the rows must land in one commit so the enum-emission audit sees both

repro: method-type-parameters/GenericMethods.cs:51 — `public T UnmanagedConstraint<T>() where T : unmanaged => default;`
secondDefectFromTriage.emitted: hasStructConstraint=false, hasClassConstraint=false, hasNotNullConstraint=false, hasConstructorConstraint=false, hasAllowRefStructConstraint=false, constraintTypeCount=0 — EVERY structured column says the parameter has no constraint at all. Only constraintText, free text, holds 'where T : unmanaged'.
secondDefectFromTriage.vocabulary: cs_type_parameter has a dedicated boolean for struct, class, notnull, new() and allows-ref-struct, and NONE for unmanaged; nor is it counted in constraintTypeCount
secondDefectFromTriage.consequence: `unmanaged` means a blittable value type holding no managed references. It IMPLIES the struct constraint, and it governs whether `fixed`, pointer types and `stackalloc` are legal on T. An engine asking 'is T a value type?' reads false from every column, and 'does T have any constraint?' reads no. The parts are right — constraintText has it — and the structure is absent.
secondDefectFromTriage.howFound: an exact reconciliation, not a hunch: Roslyn's 53 TypeConstraint nodes against our 39 + 12 left a remainder of exactly 2, and the corpus has exactly 2 unmanaged constraints
secondDefectFromTriage.owner: cs-impl — a hasUnmanagedConstraint boolean, landing with its rows so the enum-emission audit sees both
